standard.title: Angle types
standard.description: Estimate and compare angles using angle names including acute, obtuse, straight angle, reflex and revolution, and recognise their relationship to a right angle
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify angles as measures of turn and compare them with right angles (AC9M3M05). They have not yet classified angles using formal names (acute, obtuse, straight, reflex, revolution) or estimated angle sizes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students estimate and compare angles using formal angle names and recognise the relationship between each type and a right angle.

nodes.label: Classify angles by name
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex or revolution.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least four angle types from examples using a right-angle template; name each correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Classify angles in the environment and in geometric shapes using angle names; use a right-angle template to compare; explain the relationship of each type to a right angle (e.g. acute < 90°, obtuse > 90° but < 180°).
wider: Systematically classify all interior angles of a set of polygons (triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon) and record findings — noticing which shapes contain which angle types
Identify angle types in the built environment using photographs — classifying roof pitches, door hinges, ramp gradients by angle type
success_criteria: Students can correctly classify a given angle as acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex or revolution
Students can explain the relationship of each angle type to a right angle

nodes.label: Estimate and compare angles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can estimate whether angles are smaller or larger than a right angle and compare angles using a right-angle template.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a right-angle template to compare at least three angles in the environment; order them from smallest to largest.
nodes.typical_width: Estimate and compare angles in shapes and in the environment using a right-angle template; create a right-angle template and use it systematically; use tools like spirit levels and set squares to determine perpendicularity; classify angles in the environment.
wider: Use spirit levels and set squares as construction tools — investigating how right angles are used in building and carpentry, and why perpendicularity matters practically
Investigate how dynamic geometry software visualises angle measurement, exploring the relationship between rotation and angle size
success_criteria: Students can use a right-angle template to classify and compare angles in the environment
Students can order a set of angles from smallest to largest using a right-angle reference
